title: Supporting Secure Multi-GPU Computing with Dynamic and Batched Metadata Management
problem: Secure multi-GPU systems with shared memory face significant performance overhead from generating one-time pads for authenticated encryption and from security metadata such as MACs and counters consuming precious network bandwidth, exacerbated by limited OTP buffers and bursty GPU communication patterns.
motivation: Multi-GPU systems with fine-grained memory sharing are emerging for larger GPU computing problems, but securing inter-GPU and CPU-GPU communications adds substantial performance overhead that limits adoption.
method: The paper proposes dynamic OTP buffer allocation that adjusts buffer assignment per source-destination pair based on monitored communication patterns. It employs dynamic batching to transfer only a single set of metadata per batched group of data responses. The system continuously tracks communication patterns and periodically adjusts buffer sizes while dynamically forming data transfer batches.
key_novelty: Dynamic batching scheme that amortizes security metadata transfer costs across multiple batched data responses to reduce bandwidth overhead.
contributions: Dynamic OTP buffer allocation technique adapting to per-pair communication patterns
Dynamic batching scheme to reduce security metadata bandwidth consumption
Analysis of secure communication overhead in multi-GPU systems
